newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian troops patrol Recife after crime spree.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian troops patrol Recife after crime spree.

text.p: Brazilian troops took to the streets of the northeastern city of Recife on Monday to restore law and order after a surge in crime during a police strike, an official said.

"The situation is calm now, despite the refusal by police to keep up essential services," said a spokesman for the government of Pernambuco state, one of several in Brazil to be hit by a wave of police strikes.
An undisclosed number of soldiers were on patrol in the centre of Recife and in several other areas of the city including the beach neighbourhood of Boa Viagem, a popular tourist resort.

Police in Pernambuco state went on strike on July 16, prompting a surge in crime in Recife, one of Brazil's poorest cities. Gangs of youths rampaged through Boa Viagem on Saturday, a day after shops in the centre of Recife wee looted, the spokesman said.

In neighbouring Alagoas state, where troops exchanged gunfire with striking police officers last week, soldiers remained on patrol. In Sao Paulo, the country's industrial powerhouse, thousands of police officers were due to march through the city centre later on Monday to press their demands for higher pay.
